batchName: Empire: The Five Good Emperors (AD 96-192) - Easy Batch 2

questions.question: What do the spiral carvings on Trajan's Column depict?
questions.explanation: Raised in 113, Trajan's Column tells the story of the Dacian wars in spiral carvings. Tradition holds that Trajan's ashes lie in a chamber at its base.
questions.sourceQuote: In 113 he raised Trajan's Column, whose spiral carvings tell the story of the wars.

questions.question: Which city did Trajan's forces capture in 106 to end the Dacian wars?
questions.explanation: Sarmizegetusa, the Dacian capital, fell in 106. The Dacian king fled and killed himself when Roman cavalry cornered him.
questions.sourceQuote: In 106 the Romans cut the water pipes of the Dacian capital, Sarmizegetusa, and the city fell.

questions.question: In which year did the great uprising in Judaea break out under Hadrian?
questions.explanation: The revolt began in 132 under Bar Kokhba, a leader with messianic claims. At first the Romans were overwhelmed and lost heavily.
questions.sourceQuote: In 132 a massive uprising broke out in Judaea under Bar Kokhba, a leader with messianic claims.

questions.question: Which title did the Senate give Trajan, an honour no other emperor officially received?
questions.explanation: The senators called Trajan 'the best ruler', and the title appears on his coins from 105. He was the only emperor officially given it.
questions.sourceQuote: The senators rewarded him with the title 'the best ruler' (*optimus princeps*), which appears on coins from 105.

questions.question: Why did the elderly emperor Nerva adopt Trajan as his son and heir in 97?
options: He needed the army on his side
Trajan was his nephew and only relative
Trajan had saved him from an assassin
The Senate voted to impose Trajan on him
questions.explanation: Nerva had little standing with the soldiers, so he adopted a popular general. Trajan had won fame fighting Germanic tribes on the Rhine.
questions.sourceQuote: Nerva needed the army on his side.

questions.question: In 122 Hadrian ordered a famous wall built in which province?
questions.explanation: Hadrian's Wall in Britain was built by ordinary soldiers 'to separate Romans from barbarians'. Hadrian never saw it finished.
questions.sourceQuote: In Britain in 122 he ordered the wall that bears his name, built by ordinary soldiers 'to separate Romans from barbarians'.

questions.question: What fashion did Hadrian start, later copied by most emperors after him?
questions.explanation: Hadrian was the first emperor shown with a full beard. His love of Greece had earned him the nickname 'Greekling' in his youth.
questions.sourceQuote: Teased in his youth as the 'Greekling', he became the first emperor shown with a full beard, a style most later emperors copied.

questions.question: The 'Five Good Emperors' ruled Rome during which period?
questions.explanation: The five emperors from Nerva to Marcus Aurelius ruled from 96 to 180. An 18th-century English historian counted their age among the happiest in human history.
questions.sourceQuote: The label 'Five Good Emperors' covers Nerva, Trajan, Hadrian, Antoninus Pius and Marcus Aurelius, who ruled from 96 to 180.

questions.question: Against which empire did Trajan launch his last war in 113?
questions.explanation: Trajan's final war was against Parthia, the great Iranian empire beyond the Euphrates. By then he had already conquered Dacia.
questions.sourceQuote: In 113 Trajan, the emperor who had already conquered Dacia, launched his last war, against Parthia, the great Iranian empire beyond the river Euphrates.

questions.question: A Renaissance Florentine political thinker praised the five emperors as proof of what?
options: That adopting the best man beat heredity
That the Republic ought to be restored
questions.explanation: The 'Five Good Emperors' idea goes back to a Florentine thinker who argued that adoption beat hereditary succession. An English historian later popularised the phrase.
questions.sourceQuote: It goes back to a Renaissance Florentine political thinker who praised the five from Nerva to Marcus as proof that adopting the best man beat hereditary succession.
